quizzes.title: Swachh Vayu Diwas Practice Quiz
quizzes.passage:
Swachh Vayu Diwas is an occasion that draws attention to clean air and to the measures taken against air pollution. It is observed alongside an international day that the United Nations General Assembly created to strengthen awareness and international action against air pollution. The occasion is also used to recognise progress, and awards are presented to cities and wards.

The National Clean Air Programme is a national-level strategy that addresses air pollution through coordinated interventions across sectors. It covers non-attainment cities as well as million-plus cities. A non-attainment city is one that has failed to comply with national ambient air quality standards over a specified assessment period.

Progress under the programme is reviewed through the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan, an annual assessment of cities. The assessment looks at road dust management, solid waste management, vehicular emissions, industrial emissions, construction and demolition waste, commercial sources, and public awareness and outreach. Cities are evaluated on key parameters that cover air quality, action plans and institutional capacity.

Cities are grouped by population into three categories. The first covers cities above 10 lakh people, the second covers cities between 3 and 10 lakh, and the third covers cities below 3 lakh. Rankings are announced separately for each category, so cities are compared with others of similar size.

Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

questions.q: Which theme was set for the 2026 International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the 2026 theme of the International Day as 'Clean Air for Climate Action'.

questions.q: On which date was Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 observed?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was observed on 7 September 2026.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Awards were presented to cities and wards on Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026.
Reason (R): Cities and wards were recognised for demonstrating effective air pollution mitigation measures.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says the occasion marked awards to cities and wards demonstrating effective mitigation measures, so R gives the reason for A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026:
I. Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was observed on 7 September 2026.
II. The 2026 theme of the International Day is 'Breathe Life'.
III. Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was organised by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet; the 2026 theme is 'Clean Air for Climate Action' and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change organised the day.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies was designated in 2019.
II. The 2026 theme of the International Day is 'Clean Air for Climate Action'.
III. Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was observed on 2 October 2026.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while statement III gives the wrong date of 7 September 2026.

quizzes.title: Pollution Control Tools and Laws Quiz
quizzes.passage:
India uses a mix of monitoring tools, field measures and legal provisions to tackle air pollution. The National Air Quality Index communicates air quality status in terms that are easy for people to understand, and it is a tool for effective communication with the public. SAFAR, the System of Air Quality and Weather Forecast and Research, monitors city-wide and localised air quality in Indian metropolises.

Field measures also address pollution from farms. Machines such as the Turbo Happy Seeder are used in the fields, and a bio-decomposer is used to turn crop residue into manure. Emergency action is taken under the Graded Response Action Plan, a set of measures designed to prevent further deterioration of air quality. Vehicle emission standards have been implemented nationwide to reduce vehicular emissions. Both the Turbo Happy Seeder and the Pusa Bio-Decomposer are field-level tools that deal with crop residue.

The legal base includes the Air Act, the Water Act and the Environment Protection Act, which are key pollution control regulations. The Constitution also links the environment to a fundamental duty of citizens, and it has been interpreted to protect the right to a healthy environment. Monitoring, field measures, emergency action and legal provisions together make up the framework described in the booklet.

questions.q: SAFAR is an initiative of which ministry?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
questions.explanation: The booklet describes SAFAR as a Ministry of Earth Sciences initiative to monitor city-wide and localised air quality.

questions.q: In which year was Bharat Stage VI made mandatory nationwide, marking the leap from BS-IV to BS-VI?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists Bharat Stage VI as mandatory from 2020.

questions.q: Which institute developed the Pusa Bio-Decomposer, which turns crop residue into manure in 15-20 days?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Pusa Bio-Decomposer was developed by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI).

questions.q: Graded Response Action Plan measures kick in only when air quality shifts from which category to Very Poor?
questions.explanation: The booklet says GRAP measures kick in only when air quality shifts from Poor to Very Poor.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Turbo Happy Seeder can uproot stubble.
Reason (R): The Turbo Happy Seeder can also sow seeds in the area it has cleared.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but sowing seeds in the cleared area does not explain why the machine uproots stubble.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1981.
II. The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted in 1986.
III. The Environment Protection Act was enacted in 1986.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II wrongly gives 1986 for the Water Act, which was enacted in 1974.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The National Air Quality Index was introduced in 2014.
II. SAFAR is run by the Central Pollution Control Board.
III. Bharat Stage VI was made mandatory nationwide in 2020.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because SAFAR is a Ministry of Earth Sciences initiative.
